coaching.headline: Every Fangtooth, the Genesis Core and the Primal Fangtooth went to us. The tower trade was the sloppy shit.
coaching.team: We took all three Fangtooths, the Genesis Core and the Primal Fangtooth, gave up only the Mini Prime and both Seedlings, and lost only one of seven recorded fights. GRIM.exe finished with zero kills and the most deaths in the game. The towers were sloppier. After the first Fangtooth they took two of our outer towers before we took one, and after the Genesis Core the next tower to fall was our inner. We finished three towers to their four and still closed it.

focus.title: Turn the Fangtooth into a tower
focus.action: After we take a Fangtooth or the Genesis Core, call the enemy tower we hit next before anyone peels off to farm or chase. A buff that buys no structure is foreplay with no finish.

30.call: Aurora opened on Iggy & Scorch, Lt. Belica finished Serath and Greystone, and the Primal Fangtooth was ours in the same window. Three for zero, prize taken, game over. That is how to close.

10.8.call: TwinBlast opened on Serath, Lt. Belica dropped GRIM.exe and TwinBlast finished Phase, with nobody lost, in the window of our first Fangtooth. Three kills for none around a major is the standard.

21.4.call: Steel killed GRIM.exe first, Serath answered on Steel, then TwinBlast killed Serath and Grux finished Greystone. In that window we took their outer tower while one of ours also fell, so the won fight sat beside a tower trade rather than a clean gain.

27.8.call: The only fight we lost, in midmap, with no major objective falling around it. Aurora killed Serath, but Iggy & Scorch was credited with Lt. Belica and Aurora and Greystone with TwinBlast. Before taking a fight like that, name what winning it buys.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ran the hardest carry game in the lobby: the most kills and the most hero damage in the game, plus first blood. TwinBlast killed Serath three times and Phase twice. That is a carry doing carry shit.
Phase killed TwinBlast in both early deaths. Energy Lance roots once the beam has stacked long enough, so when the beam lands on TwinBlast, Rocket Dash out early instead of trading through it.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs ran a fucking tank-support clinic. Steel mitigated more damage than anyone in the game, had a hand in half our kills, placed more wards than the recorded norm and died once, inside a fight we won.

In the midmap fight we lost, Iggy & Scorch was credited with Lt. Belica and Aurora. Force Shield blocks enemy projectiles, so when the Flame Turrets go down, put the wall between the turret fire and Lt. Belica.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster did the most objective damage in the game by a mile and cleared the most enemy wards. Aurora also took kills in both late fights, two of them in the only fight we lost.

Serath is immune to crowd control and invulnerable during Heaven's Fury, then reappears on the marked target. When Serath marks Aurora or a nearby ally, hold Hoarfrost for that landing instead of wasting the root on an untouchable target.
59bc2b4e-5cc2-4e4f-9dda-9fae3f686f78: Lt. Belica finished Serath and Greystone in the Primal Fangtooth window, killed Iggy & Scorch twice in the midgame and died only twice. Farm ran above the recorded norm. Tidy, efficient mid work.

Neural Disruptor resets at max rank if the target dies shortly after the blast, and both Eternal minors feed the ultimate. In a won fight, fire it at the lowest target first so the reset can chain a second kill.
dfc1532a-f881-4efe-a48b-df67882e88f7: Grux hit hard: hero damage per minute ran far above the recorded norm, Greystone died to Grux twice, and only Aurora took more damage on our team. A bleeding brick wall with a grudge.

Greystone killed Grux all three times, twice before the ten-minute mark. When Greystone enters Stone Forged Soul, step out of the slow before the crash lands instead of swinging at a statue that is healing.

matchup: GRIM.exe deals magical basic attacks and Energy Shield blocks one incoming ability; Phase roots and blinds.
Greystone was their top damage dealer, and Serath's Heaven's Fury reaches a marked target while immune to crowd control.
build: Solaris pairs with Gunslinger's triple shot after each cast.
Tainted Rounds had targets: Phase, Serath and Greystone each healed heavily.
eternal: This setup suits a carry finishing low targets; Rocket Dash and Pacifier both trigger Wind-Rider.
Natural Resistance is the draft alternative to Forage if crowd control is the main threat, trading farm income for a cleanse.
augment: Grenadier's extra grenades are extra casts, feeding Gunslinger and Solaris, though Solaris has a short internal cooldown.
Spray 'N Pray is the alternative, trading grenade uptime for a stronger Ventilate that loses accuracy at range.
crest: Pacifier's empowered hit pairs with Vaporize and Ventilate, and the dash also triggers Wind-Rider.
improvement: Vanquisher is a sound keep: Greystone's passive armor, Phase's Vanguardian and Golem's Gift gave its penetration targets.
Ashbringer is the swap when reachable targets are squishy, trading penetration and execute for more grenades, dashes and Gunslinger shots.

matchup: Phase was the enemy's listed healer, and GRIM.exe's Displacement Blast pushes heroes away.
Serath's Heaven's Fury dives while immune to crowd control; Serath killed Steel inside a fight we won.
build: Dynamo pays off Steel's stuns, and Tainted Guard triggers on GRIM.exe, Serath and Greystone basic attacks.
Only Xenia adds magical armor against the enemy's three magical damage dealers.
eternal: Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue, trading out-of-combat regeneration for anti-heal on Phase, Serath and Greystone.
augment: Heavy Metal is fed by Xenia, Dynamo and Tainted Guard, which all add armor.
Colossal Crash is the alternative for a longer, wider Shield Slam, giving up the knockup for a knockback.
crest: Sanctification's shield and tenacity matter against Phase's root and slows from Greystone and Serath.
Steel placed more wards than the recorded norm.
improvement: Steel had the most mitigation in the game and one death, so the current three items are a sound keep.
Tainted Charm is the swap if enemy healing starts deciding fights, giving up Tainted Guard's armor and some Heavy Metal damage.

matchup: Serath dives a marked target while immune to crowd control and builds for basic-attack damage and lifesteal.
Aurora's kills landed on GRIM.exe and Iggy & Scorch twice each and on Serath once.
build: Hoarfrost, Glacial Thorns and Cryoseism give the immobilize passives plenty of triggers.
Nothing adds magical armor against Iggy & Scorch, GRIM.exe and Phase.
eternal: This setup suits close-range spell fighting.
Immaculate is the draft alternative to Fragrance, trading damage for damage reduction near full health.
augment: Glacial Thorns adds another root, feeding Spectral Schematics, Dynamo and Frozen Simulacrum cooldown reduction.
Hypothermia is the alternative to slow Serath's and Greystone's basic attacks, giving up the extra root.
crest: Iggy & Scorch's Tainted Scepter means its heal is not guaranteed in every fight.
improvement: With two deaths and the most objective damage in the game, the current build is a sound keep.
If Iggy & Scorch's magic starts ending fights, Unbroken Will is the comparison, trading Dynamo's physical armor for magical armor and tenacity.

matchup: Iggy & Scorch zones with fire and runs on mana, so Void Drone and Neural Disruptor have a target.
Serath and Iggy & Scorch each killed Lt. Belica once.
build: Seismic Assault into Void Bomb or Neural Disruptor is the natural Noxia sequence.
eternal: The Tenth Seal and Millennia both add ultimate damage, so both minors lean on Neural Disruptor.
Tithe of Death is the draft alternative to The Tenth Seal, trading ultimate uptime for mana and stacking ability haste on takedowns.
augment: Combat Veteran helps reach maxed abilities and Innovation upgrades sooner.
Devastating Bombs is the alternative when targets are often alone, at the cost of the experience and speed.
crest: Epoch buys time against Serath's dive or Inferno while teammates react.
It provides no escape distance; Lt. Belica stays in place.
improvement: No build change is proven here; this is the winning core plus Oblivion Crown, otherwise a sound keep.
If spells bounce off a front line with Phase's Vanguardian, Magnify is the later-slot comparison, trading raw power for penetration.

matchup: Greystone was the enemy's top damage dealer and killed Grux all three times; Grux killed Greystone twice.
Stoicism grows Greystone's regeneration and armor as health drops, and Make Way shreds physical armor.
build: Basilisk's armor shred matters against Stoicism's armor.
None of the four items adds physical or magical armor.
eternal: This setup rewards staying in long brawls.
Taste of Iron is the draft alternative to Leech, trading the regeneration cut for a damage boost on Bloodlust's bleed.
augment: Red Mist pays off in team brawls where several heroes are bleeding.
Lust For Blood is the sustain alternative, giving up the attack speed.
crest: Razorback answers Greystone's physical damage in an extended trade.
improvement: Greystone killed Grux three times while Grux carried no armor item.
If Greystone keeps landing those kills, a physical-armor slot such as Stonewall is the comparison, trading damage for survival.
The winning core's Augmentation trades Terminus' critical chance and lifesteal shield for health, haste and an empowered attack.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Phase. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s), Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Vortex Grenade → Vaporize pierce → Rocket Dash reposition → Ventilate ult
ourKits.winCondition: reposition with Rocket Dash and unload Ventilate from safety
ourKits.passive: abilities grant AS + a triple-shot next basic
ourKits.playWith: a frontline to create his free-fire window
ourKits.playAgainst: he's mobile but squishy — CC through the dash, then burst

ourKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
ourKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
ourKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
ourKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start

ourKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
ourKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
ourKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
ourKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Telekinetic Link an ally → Psychic Flare blind → Energy Lance → Hyperflux buff ult
enemyKits.winCondition: buff a hyper-carry through the Link and Hyperflux for a teamfight
enemyKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally
enemyKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
enemyKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

enemyKits.combo: Energy Shield block → Displacement Blast → Assault Mode → GTFO lockon ult
enemyKits.winCondition: out-trade with Pulsefire and the spell-shield, finish with GTFO
enemyKits.playWith: peel so he can free-cast in Assault Mode
enemyKits.playAgainst: bait Energy Shield, then commit; dodge GTFO's slow channel

enemyKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
enemyKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
enemyKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

greystone.loadout: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity), augment Close Cut, crest Judgement
lines: Stone Forged Soul at rank 3: 145s base, about 103.6s by the end (29% shorter) from 40 ability haste: Augmentation 20, Basilisk 20.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Greystone dealt 23,965 hero damage, 29% of their team's, with +157 physical power from items.
Overlord (item): On Successful Basic Attack: Deal (+1%) Damage. Deal (+30%) (+2.5%) Damage around the Target. Damage decreases from 100% to 50% based on distance.
Augmentation (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal (+90% Base Physical Power) Damage On-Hit.
Judgement (crest): Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.

Thraex (Eternal): Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).
Close Cut (augment): Make Way deals 20% increased damage to the nearest Enemy Unit.

Sustain: 4% omnivamp; Salvation: On going below 30% Health: Gain a (+25%) Shield for 6s. Reduced to 50% Effectiveness for Ranged Heroes. Gain 10% Omnivamp for 6s.; Judgement: Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.; Savage Strikes: Deal 1.5 (+0.4 per level) Physical Damage On-Hit. Attacking an Enemy Hero increases this by 100% for 3s, stacking up to 3 times. Heal for the damage dealt.; 11,952 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1275 health, +25% tenacity; took 46,775 damage, mitigated 34,979, died 3 times.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 4 effects on one trigger: Overlord, Augmentation, Thraex, Savage Strikes.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 3 effects on one trigger: Salvation, Judgement, Savage Strikes.
The Eternal was part of it: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) sits on the same triggers as the items (every basic attack set off; healing off the damage), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 0 of the 2 players Greystone killed built physical armor. Anti-heal on TwinBlast, Steel. We killed Greystone 3 times.

Copy it? Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity): 50.3% in 2,224 Greystone offlane games, below the hero's 51.9%; this 3-item core: 54.3% in 173 games, below the 57.6% of that hero-role's cores. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

card.lesson: Stone Forged Soul came back about every 104s instead of 145s by the end (29% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.

twinblast.loadout: Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider), augment Grenadier, crest Pacifier
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,130 hero damage a minute, more than 75% of TwinBlast carry players this patch (31% of the team's). The damage came from Solaris, Tainted Rounds, Imperator.
Ventilate at rank 3: 85s base, about 77.3s by the end (9% shorter) from 10 ability haste: Solaris 10.
TwinBlast dealt 35,030 hero damage, 31% of their team's, with +212 physical power from items.

Penetration: Vanquisher 12; against Serath (level 16: about 104 physical armor, 92 after penetration; took 5,773 physical damage from heroes, 41% of all hero damage they took) and GRIM.exe (level 16: about 110 physical armor, 98 after penetration; took 9,671 physical damage from heroes, 45% of all hero damage they took) that is about 6% and 6% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Solaris (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal 45 (+35%) Damage On-Hit. Can Critically Strike. Heals you for 50% of damage dealt.
Tainted Rounds (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 3s. Deal (+10%) (+20%) Damage On-Hit. Increases by up to 100% as the Target's Health decreases.
Imperator (item): Critical Strikes deal 30% more damage.
Pacifier (crest): Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health.
Weald (Eternal): Damaging an Enemy Hero below 30% Health fires 4 (+1 per 30% Bonus Attack Speed) projectiles that each deal 7 (+1 per level) True Damage.

Sustain: 7% lifesteal; Solaris: On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal 45 (+35%) Damage On-Hit. Can Critically Strike. Heals you for 50% of damage dealt.; Tainted Rounds: On Successful Basic Attacks: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 3s. Deal (+10%) (+20%) Damage On-Hit. Increases by up to 100% as the Target's Health decreases.; 5,706 healing recorded.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Solaris, Tainted Rounds, Weald.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 3 effects on one trigger: Solaris, Tainted Rounds, Pacifier.
Stack (Finishing damage on low-health targets): 2 effects on one trigger: Vanquisher, Weald. Once a fight started going their way, these finished it.
The Eternal was part of it: Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider) sits on the same triggers as the items (every basic attack set off; finishing damage on low-health targets), so the same hits paid out twice.
Countered? 1 of the 4 players TwinBlast killed built physical armor (Phase). Anti-heal on Iggy & Scorch. We killed TwinBlast 3 times.

Copy it? Weald (Forage + Wind-Rider): 52.1% in 1,306 TwinBlast carry games, above the hero's 50.3%; this 3-item core: 56.7% in 543 games, above the 55.3% of that hero-role's cores. Proven this patch: worth copying.
